question: According to the Basic Control Skills scoring rules, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_b: Coming to a complete stop without changing direction
choice_c: Touching a boundary cone with the vehicle's mirror
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual states pull-ups are pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position, scored on Exercise 2 and Exercise 4.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Pull-Ups)

question: Pull-ups are scored on which two Basic Control Skills exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_c: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
explanation: The manual specifically identifies Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing) as the exercises where pull-ups are scored.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Pull-Ups)

question: Per the manual, does simply stopping without changing direction count as a pull-up?
choice_a: Yes, but only during Exercise 4
choice_b: Yes, any stop during a backing exercise counts as a pull-up
choice_c: No, stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up
choice_d: No, but it counts as an encroachment instead
explanation: The manual explicitly states, "Stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Pull-Ups)

question: How does the examiner treat your first pull-ups during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Any pull-up at all results in an automatic failure
choice_b: Only pull-ups after a "look" are penalized
choice_c: Pull-ups are never scored under any circumstance
choice_d: You are not penalized for initial pull-ups, but an excessive number will count as errors
explanation: The manual states, "You will not be penalized for initial pull-ups. However, an excessive number of pull-ups, will count as errors."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Pull-Ups)

question: What is scored as an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique parts at/above door mirror height
choice_b: Pulling forward to correct your position in the alley
choice_c: Sounding the horn before completing the exercise
choice_d: Exiting the vehicle to check its position from outside
explanation: The manual defines an encroachment as touching or crossing over an exercise boundary line or cone with any part of the vehicle other than the mirrors or unique vehicle parts at or higher than door mirror height.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Encroachments)

question: If you encroach on a boundary during a backing exercise, what must you do?
choice_a: Continue the exercise and report it to the examiner afterward
choice_b: Stop immediately when signaled by the examiner and return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries
choice_c: Automatically fail the test with no opportunity to continue
choice_d: Exit the vehicle to reposition the cones
explanation: The manual states that if you have encroached, the examiner will stop you and you must return the vehicle within the exercise boundaries, stopping immediately when signaled.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Encroachments)

question: What does the manual define as a "look" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Checking your mirrors while driving forward
choice_b: Glancing over your shoulder while backing without stopping
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's external position while backing
choice_d: Asking the examiner a clarifying question before starting
explanation: The manual defines a "look" as exiting the vehicle while performing an exercise to check the vehicle's position while backing.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Looks)

question: Before safely exiting the vehicle to check its position during a backing exercise, what must you do?
choice_a: Turn off the engine completely
choice_b: Sound the horn twice
choice_c: Ask the examiner to exit the vehicle first
choice_d: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park
explanation: The manual requires that when exiting to check the vehicle's position, you must set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park, then exit safely while facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Looks)

question: On a bus, what specific action counts as a "look" during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Walking to the back of the bus to get a better view
choice_b: Adjusting the side mirrors while stopped
choice_c: Opening the driver's window
choice_d: Honking the horn before backing
explanation: The manual states that on a bus, if you walk to the back of the bus to get a better view, it will count as a "look."
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Looks)

question: What may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Taking a free look within the allowed limit
choice_b: Opening your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park)
choice_c: Using more than one pull-up
choice_d: Asking the examiner for clarification on instructions
explanation: The manual warns that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving (not in neutral and park), it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Looks)

question: How many free looks are you permitted on Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), respectively?
choice_a: Two free looks on Exercise 2 and one on Exercise 4
choice_b: Zero free looks on either exercise
choice_c: One free look on Exercise 2 and two free looks on Exercise 4
choice_d: Three free looks on each exercise
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Looks)

question: Final vehicle position is scored on which exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 1 (Forward Stop) and Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)
choice_b: All four exercises equally
choice_c: Only Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
choice_d: Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing) and Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing)
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Final Position)

question: Upon completing an exercise, what must you do to indicate you have finished?
choice_a: Set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn
choice_b: Wave to the examiner
choice_c: Turn off the vehicle entirely
choice_d: Open the door and step out
explanation: The manual instructs that upon completion of an exercise, you should set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn indicating you have completed the exercise.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Exercise Completion Procedure)

question: What can happen if you fail to follow the examiner's instructions for completing an exercise as directed?
choice_a: You receive a warning but may continue
choice_b: It may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_c: Only the specific exercise is repeated
choice_d: Nothing, as long as final position is correct
explanation: The manual states that failure to follow examiner instructions for completing the exercise as directed may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.1, Scoring (Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act)

question: In Exercise 1 (Forward Stop), what must you do?
choice_a: Back straight through an alley until clearing the last cones
choice_b: Offset back into an alley and stop within three feet of the rear boundary
choice_c: Drive forward through the alley and stop with the front-most part of the vehicle within the box at the end, without going past it, stopping only once
choice_d: Steer left through an opening into the opposite lane without stopping
explanation: Exercise 1 requires driving forward through the alley and stopping with the front-most part of the vehicle within the box at the end of the alley without going past it, and you may stop only once.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.1, Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: For Exercise 2 (Straight-Line Backing), how many free pull-ups and vehicle exits (looks) are you allowed?
choice_a: Two free pull-ups and two free exits
choice_b: No free pull-ups but unlimited exits
choice_c: Three free pull-ups and no exits
choice_d: One free pull-up and one free exit to check around the vehicle
explanation: The manual states for Exercise 2, you are allowed one free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one time to check around the vehicle.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.2, Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing

question: What are you not allowed to do during Exercise 3 (Forward Offset Tracking)?
choice_a: Stop, back up, or exit the vehicle; if you stop, the exercise will be ended
choice_b: Use your turn signals
choice_c: Shift gears at any point
choice_d: Check your mirrors
explanation: The manual states you are NOT allowed to stop, back up, or exit the vehicle during Exercise 3; if you stop, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.3, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 (Reverse Offset Backing), how close must the rear-most part of the vehicle come to the rear of the alley?
choice_a: Within one foot
choice_b: Within three feet
choice_c: Within ten feet
choice_d: It must not come within any specified distance
explanation: The manual states you must bring the rear-most part of your vehicle within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box at the end.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: If you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4, what must you do?
choice_a: Immediately end the exercise as a failure
choice_b: Continue backing until told to stop
choice_c: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance until signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise
choice_d: Exit the vehicle to check the boundary
explanation: The manual states that if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance until you are signaled by the examiner to stop, prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.4, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must happen before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: You must complete a written retest
choice_b: You must demonstrate railroad crossing procedures
choice_c: You must complete a pre-trip inspection
choice_d: You must pass the Basic Control Skills test
explanation: The manual states, under Road Test, that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 12.2.4, Road Test

question: During the on-road driving test, what must you do at all times?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs/signals/laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_b: Maintain maximum legal speed at all times
choice_c: Use the horn before every turn
choice_d: Keep the vehicle in the leftmost lane
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test, you must drive safely and must wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not include a certain traffic situation, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Skip that portion of scoring entirely
choice_b: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_c: Automatically receive full credit
choice_d: Drive to a different test route
explanation: The manual states that if your route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate them by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing in that situation.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1, How You Will Be Tested

question: Before making a turn, what must you do?
choice_a: Accelerate through the turn
choice_b: Signal only if other vehicles are present
choice_c: Check traffic in all directions
choice_d: Shift into neutral
explanation: The manual lists checking traffic in all directions as the first requirement when you have been asked to make a turn.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: According to the manual, when does "unsafe coasting" occur?
choice_a: Whenever the vehicle exceeds the speed limit
choice_b: Whenever the driver removes a hand from the steering wheel
choice_c: When brakes are applied before shifting
choice_d: When the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of your vehicle.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.1, Turns

question: While stopped at an intersection behind a stop sign or signal, what is required of your vehicle?
choice_a: It must not roll forward or backward
choice_b: It must be shifted into park immediately
choice_c: It must sound the horn
choice_d: The parking brake must always be set
explanation: The manual states that as you approach an intersection and come to a complete stop, your vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: What must you avoid doing while driving through an intersection?
choice_a: Checking your mirrors
choice_b: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_c: Yielding to pedestrians
choice_d: Decelerating
explanation: The manual instructs that when driving through an intersection, you should not change lanes while proceeding through it.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.2, Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the test, where should your vehicle be positioned?
choice_a: As far left as possible to avoid pedestrians
choice_b: Straddling two lanes for visibility
choice_c: Centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), keeping up with traffic flow without exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_d: In the center turn lane whenever available
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.3, Urban Business

question: What is the proper procedure for changing lanes during the test?
choice_a: Change lanes immediately, then check mirrors afterward
choice_b: Use hazard lights instead of turn signals
choice_c: Change lanes only when directed verbally without checking traffic
choice_d: Make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when it is safe to do so.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.4, Lane Changes

question: Before entering an expressway, what must you do?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic
choice_b: Come to a complete stop
choice_c: Activate four-way flashers
choice_d: Downshift to first gear
explanation: The manual lists checking traffic, using proper signals, and merging smoothly into the proper lane of traffic as the required steps before entering the expressway.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the exit ramp of an expressway, what must you continue to do?
choice_a: Accelerate to match highway speed
choice_b: Decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles
choice_c: Change lanes as needed to find the fastest exit
choice_d: Activate your left turn signal
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.5, Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: For the Stop/Start maneuver, what are you asked to do?
choice_a: Make a U-turn and return to the starting point
choice_b: Perform a three-point turn
choice_c: Pull the vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if you were going to get out and check something on the vehicle
choice_d: Parallel park between two vehicles
explanation: The manual states that for this maneuver, you will be asked to pull your vehicle over to the side of the road and stop as if you were going to get out and check something on your vehicle.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: Once stopped during the Stop/Start maneuver, what must your vehicle position be?
choice_a: Perpendicular to the curb for maximum visibility
choice_b: At least one full lane width from the curb
choice_c: Positioned with hazard lights off
choice_d: Parallel to the curb or shoulder of the road and safely out of the traffic flow, not blocking driveways, hydrants, etc.
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, the vehicle must be parallel to the curb or shoulder of the road and safely out of the traffic flow, and should not be blocking driveways, fire hydrants, intersections, or signs.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: When instructed to resume from the Stop/Start maneuver, what should you NOT do until your vehicle actually moves?
choice_a: Turn the wheel before your vehicle moves
choice_b: Check your mirrors
choice_c: Release the parking brake
choice_d: Activate the left turn signal
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs, "Do not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves" when resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.6, Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?
choice_a: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_b: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_c: Shift into neutral
choice_d: Move to the outer edge of the lane
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.7, Curve

question: What must you avoid doing while any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Checking traffic in all directions
choice_b: Keeping your hands on the steering wheel
choice_c: Stopping, changing gears, passing another vehicle, or changing lanes
choice_d: Maintaining your current speed
explanation: The manual states not to stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: For buses, school buses, or vehicles displaying placards, within what distance from the nearest rail must the vehicle stop at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: Within 100 feet but not less than 25 feet
choice_b: Exactly at the rail itself
choice_c: Within 20 feet but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual instructs such drivers to stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: When must a driver of a placarded vehicle activate the four-way flashers at a railroad crossing?
choice_a: As the vehicle approaches the railroad crossing, deactivating them after the vehicle crosses
choice_b: Only after crossing the tracks
choice_c: Only if a train is visible
choice_d: Four-way flashers are not required at railroad crossings
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, activate the four-way flashers, which should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.8, Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the test, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The manufacturer of the overpass
choice_b: The posted clearance or height of the overpass
choice_c: The weight of your own vehicle
choice_d: The exact date the overpass was built
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.9, Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: When stopping a school bus for student discharge, how far away from the students at the stop must the bus come to a complete stop?
choice_a: At least 25 feet away
choice_b: At least 5 feet away
choice_c: At least 10 feet away
choice_d: There is no minimum distance specified
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.10, Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Under the General Driving Behaviors scoring categories, which of the following is required?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed on grades
choice_b: Braking harshly to ensure a complete stop
choice_c: Keeping only one hand on the steering wheel while driving straight
choice_d: Double-clutching when shifting an unsynchronized manual transmission, and not shifting gears while in turns or intersections
explanation: The manual requires that if equipped with an unsynchronized manual transmission, you must double-clutch when shifting, and under Gear Usage, you should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: South Carolina Commercial Driver License Manual (Version: March 2025, AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System base content), South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) -- Section 13.1.11(a) Clutch Usage and 13.1.12(b) Gear Usage
